hypothesis: If Darwin is right, then among oceanic islands (never joined to a continent), nearly all that are large enough to hold a resident fauna have at least one native bat record in GBIF, and a substantial share of the remote ones have bat taxa that occur nowhere else.
pass_criterion: Sample: every oceanic island or archipelago with land area >=100 km2 (volcanic or coral origin, never land-connected), taken from a list fixed before querying, N>=40. Query GBIF for Chiroptera (taxonKey 734) records on each, excluding records with establishmentMeans of INTRODUCED, INVASIVE or MANAGED and excluding fossil or living-specimen basis of record. Pass if BOTH hold: (a) >=80% of sampled islands have >=1 native bat species; and (b) among islands >=500 km from the nearest continent, >=30% have >=1 bat species or subspecies recorded only from that island or archipelago, checked against the IUCN range or the GBIF species-level distribution.
fail_criterion: Fail if either (a) <60% of sampled islands have a native bat record, or (b) <15% of islands >=500 km from the nearest continent have an endemic bat taxon. Results between the pass and fail thresholds count as inconclusive and partially supportive only.
interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic islands' means islands far from continents and never connected to one, which is roughly the modern oceanic or volcanic island category. 'Ærial mammals' means Chiroptera. 'Almost every island' is operationalised as >=80% of islands of at least 100 km2, because tiny islets cannot be expected to hold resident mammals. 'Often endemic' is operationalised as >=30% of remote islands, and endemism is counted at the species or subspecies level. Modern reinterpretation: GBIF records are sampling-biased, and absence of a record is weak evidence of absence, so the island list must be cross-checked against the IUCN range for any island with no GBIF bat record. Introduced taxa are excluded. Vagrant single records are excluded unless they come from a resident population.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (search and download service, filtered to Chiroptera, taxonKey 734)
dataset.why_it_fits: GBIF serves occurrence records through a public API (https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search). The fields used would be taxonKey or order=Chiroptera, scientificName, species, country or countryCode, islandGroup, island, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord and occurrenceStatus. These let us count native bat species per island and identify species restricted to a single island or archipelago. Any download gets its own citable DOI, which is why the dataset-level DOI above is null.
